snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹30 lakh–1.5 crore for your own manufacturing and B2B supply
snapshot.distribution_note: B2B buyers and conscious consumers; price is the main barrier

tailwinds: India's single-use plastic ban has created demand for alternatives.
Companies need sustainable packaging to meet EPR and ESG goals.
Bamboo, jute and agricultural waste are cheap raw materials.
headwinds: Eco products usually cost more than plastic.
Enforcement of plastic bans is uneven.
angle_2026: Plastic bans and EPR rules have made sustainable packaging a business need, not just a preference. In 2026, eco brands grow by selling to businesses that must meet rules, and by making products that match plastic on price and quality.
cost_basis: Estimated for a brand sourcing from manufacturers and selling to consumers and businesses, 2026 prices.

unit_economics.example: For a ₹500 eco product sold online:
unit_economics.note: Bulk orders from businesses have lower margins but no ad costs.

investor_probes: Can your product match plastic on price?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start with one product for business buyers who must replace plastic, then build a consumer brand.
sourcing_edge: Bamboo from Assam and Tripura, jute from West Bengal, areca leaves from Karnataka and bagasse from sugar mills are cheap raw materials.
licences: Compostability certification (CIPET or similar) for compostable claims
Plastic Waste Management and EPR registration where relevant

hard_truths.title: Price gap
hard_truths.text: Eco products usually cost more. Target buyers who must switch or value sustainability.

hard_truths.title: Greenwashing
hard_truths.text: Unproven claims damage trust. Certify your claims.

hard_truths.title: Quality
hard_truths.text: Natural materials vary. Test every batch.

hard_truths.title: Enforcement
hard_truths.text: Plastic bans aren't always enforced. Don't rely on regulation alone.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹1.5 lakh in sales, including one business buyer.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Decide on B2B or B2C focus.
